newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power up on outage, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power up on outage, short-covering.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region rose Thursday amid outage of Duke Power Co's McGuire nuclear units and short-covering of November physical positions, brokers and marketers said.
"People are scrambling. People here are short," a Houston trader.
Duke's McGuire units 1 and 2 in Cornelius, N.C., each rated at 1,129 megawatt (MW), were expected to be idled for at least three weeks, while awaiting a replacement battery bank.

"It's certainly affecting it like it was," a East Coast broker noted the bullish effect of the McGuire outage on the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, although the McGuire units are not in the PJM district.
Meanwhile, the 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit, which was shut Monday to repair a steam drain pipe leak, was scheduled to resume service early next week.
The 610 MW Oyster Creek nuclear power plant, idled since last Friday, was also expected to return to operation early next week.

The Overall tenor of the PJM market has been underpinned by firm natural gas prices and ongoing transmission constraint to Philadelphia and northern New Jersey due to limited operation of the Whitpain substation.
The substation, operated by PECO Energy Co, was damaged by a fire earlier this month.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Friday was quoted at $25.75-$26.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), up sharply from Wednesday's $24.75-$25.50.
November PJM electricity for firm, peak delivery was assessed at $24.25-$24.75, higher than Wednesday's range of $23.75-$24.50. November firm, off-peak delivery was valued near $18.00.
December PJM power with similar delivery conditions was discussed between $28.60 and $29.00, better bid than Wednesday's quote of $28.30-$29.00.
January/February 1997 PJM deliveries were pegged at $32.50-$32.75, up from $32.15-$32.50 on Wednesday.
First-quarter 1997 PJM electricity were assessed near $29.75, compared with Wednesday's $29.60-$30.00.
July/August 1997 PJM power was discussed at $31.75-$32.00.
